raw_text:
Below is a structured 12-week program tailored for a 47-year-old female advanced lifter in early perimenopause with irregular cycles, significant heat tolerance issues, and a priority on bone-loading compound lifts. The plan emphasizes bone density preservation/gain, muscular strength, and pragmatic cooling strategies. It avoids sauna/fasted high-intensity sessions in heated environments and builds a structured cooling protocol after hard sessions.

Key assumptions and goals
- Training frequency: 4 days/week (adjustable if needed)
- Primary goal: bone-loading compound movements with progressive overload; maintain/rebuild lean mass; manage heat sensitivity
- Heat management: all sessions in a climate-controlled gym, avoid high heat/high humidity; explicit cooling protocols post-workout; hydration plan
- Periodization: 12 weeks with 3 phases (Foundation/Adaptation, Progressive Loading, Peak/Consolidation)
- Menopause/menstrual irregularities: exercise programming remains consistent; monitor signs, adjust intensities if symptoms spike
- Nutrition support: emphasis on adequate protein, calcium/vitamin D intake, hydration, and peri-workout fueling; consider intake around workouts to support performance and recovery

General guidelines for all sessions
- Warm-up: 10–12 minutes dynamic mobility, activation, and light cardio
- Rest periods: 2–3 minutes for heavy compound lifts; 1–2 minutes for accessory work
- Tempo: emphasis on controlled eccentric actions (e.g., 2–0–2–1 when appropriate) to maximize bone-loading stimulus
- Technique: prioritize form, especially with heavier loads; use a spotter or safety racks for squats/bench/deadlift
- Cooling after sessions: 15–20 minutes of active cooling (low-intensity cycling or walking at 60–70% HR max), cold towels, and shaded area; ensure ambient room cooling and hydration
- Hydration: aim for 250–500 ml water during warm-ups, and 500–750 ml per hour during training depending on sweat rate; electrolytes if sessions >60 minutes
- Heat management: avoid training in hot environments; if symptoms flare, reduce load/volume and switch to lower-intensity, cooler sessions

12-week plan overview and progression
Phase 1: Foundation/Adaptation (Weeks 1–4)
- Focus: re-establish technique, build bone-loading stimulus with heavy compound lifts at controlled intensities, introduce structured cooling
- Weekly structure: 4 days (e.g., Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat)
- Core lifts: squat, deadlift, press variations, hip hinge
- Accessory work: aimed at glute/hamstring emphasis, upper back, core stability
- Reps/sets: solid loading with lower rep ranges for main lifts; accessory volume moderate

Phase 2: Progressive Loading (Weeks 5–8)
- Focus: progressive overload across main lifts, maintain bone-loading stimulus, refine technique under heavier loads
- Weekly structure: 4 days
- Adjusted progression: add microcycle progression (load increments every 1–2 weeks), slight rep reductions if needed
- Conditioning: maintain low-impact conditioning or mobility work to support recovery

Phase 3: Peak/Consolidation (Weeks 9–12)
- Focus: peak strength in main lifts, consolidate gains, fine-tune fatigue management
- Weekly structure: 4 days
- Intensity: approach 85–90% ə of 1RM for main lifts with controlled volume
- Taper: slight reduction in volume in Weeks 11–12 to allow full recovery

Detailed week-by-week plan
Weeks 1–4 (Phase 1: Foundation/Adaptation)

Weekly framework (4 sessions)
- Day A: Squat focus + upper back/arm accessory
- Day B: Hip hinge (deadlift) focus + posterior chain/accessory
- Day C: Push strength (bench/overhead press) + core
- Day D: Full-body with emphasis on hip drive and pull

Week 1
- Main lifts:
  - Squat: 4x5 at 75% 1RM
  - Deadlift (conventional or sumo): 4x5 at 75% 1RM
  - Bench press: 3x6 at 70% 1RM
  - Overhead press: 3x6 at 70% 1RM
- Accessory (choose 2–3 per day):
  - Hip thrust or glute bridge: 3x8
  - Pendlay rows or barbell rows: 3x8
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3x8 per leg
  - Lateral raises: 2x12
  - Pallof press or other anti-rotation: 3x10
- Core: planks 3x30–45s
- Conditioning: 10 minutes light cardio
- Cooling protocol: post-workout 15–20 min active cooling; cold towels; hydration

Week 2
- Increase main lifts by 2.5–5% depending on comfort
- Squat: 4x5 at 77–78% 1RM
- Deadlift: 4x5 at 77–78% 1RM
- Bench: 3x6 at 72–74% 1RM
- Overhead press: 3x6 at 72–74% 1RM
- Accessory: similar, add one more set on one exercise or increase reps by 1
- Core and conditioning: same approach, maintain cooling protocol

Week 3
- Deload-lite? No, keep moderate load
- Squat: 4x5 at 75–78% 1RM
- Deadlift: 4x5 at 75–78% 1RM
- Bench: 3x6 at 72–75% 1RM
- Overhead press: 3x6 at 72–75% 1RM
- Accessory: keep volume, can swap for tempo sets (2–0–2–1)
- Focus on technique; record lift cues; ensure cooling

Week 4
- Load progression, target 80% region for main lifts
- Squat: 4x4 at 80% 1RM
- Deadlift: 4x4 at 80% 1RM
- Bench: 3x5 at 75–77% 1RM
- Overhead press: 3x5 at 75–77% 1RM
- Accessory: 3–4 exercises, 3x8
- Recovery emphasis: nutrition, sleep, cooling

Weeks 5–8 (Phase 2: Progressive Loading)

Week 5
- Ramping: add 2.5–5% to main lifts where tolerated
- Squat: 5x4 at 80% 1RM
- Deadlift: 5x4 at 80% 1RM
- Bench: 4x6 at 72–75% 1RM
- Overhead press: 4x6 at 72–75% 1RM
- Accessory: emphasize posterior chain, core stability
- Conditioning: 10–15 min low-intensity cardio
- Cooling: ensure post-workout cooling and hydration

Week 6
- Slight progression
- Squat: 5x3 at 82–85% 1RM
- Deadlift: 5x3 at 82–85% 1RM
- Bench: 4x5 at 77–79% 1RM
- Overhead press: 4x5 at 77–79% 1RM
- Accessory: carry higher reps on glute hinge and rows
- Core: 3x12 carries or farmer walks 2x30s

Week 7
- Benchmark-like week: maintain or slightly reduce loads to allow adaptation
- Squat: 4x5 at 78–82% 1RM
- Deadlift: 4x5 at 78–82% 1RM
- Bench: 3x5 at 75–78% 1RM
- Overhead press: 3x5 at 75–78% 1RM
- Accessory: same pattern, emphasize control
- Cooling protocol reinforced

Week 8
- Peak-ish loading week
- Squat: 4x4 at 82% 1RM
- Deadlift: 4x4 at 82% 1RM
- Bench: 3x5 at 80% 1RM
- Overhead press: 3x5 at 80% 1RM
- Accessory: 3x8 high-quality reps
- Recovery focus: hydration and sleep; note any symptoms

Weeks 9–12 (Phase 3: Peak/Consolidation)

Week 9
- Intensify slightly while maintaining form
- Squat: 3x3 at 85% 1RM
- Deadlift: 3x3 at 85% 1RM
- Bench: 3x4 at 82% 1RM
- Overhead press: 3x4 at 82% 1RM
- Accessory: 2–3 exercises, 3x6–8
- Cooling: keep strict cooling; consider adding 5–10 minutes of light mobility work post

Week 10
- Maintain high intensity with managed volume
- Squat: 3x3 at 87% 1RM
- Deadlift: 3x3 at 87% 1RM
- Bench: 3x4 at 80–82% 1RM
- Overhead press: 3x4 at 80–82% 1RM
- Accessory: 2–3 exercises; keep reps moderate
- Recovery: nutrition + sleep emphasis

Week 11
- Taper in volume, maintain intensity
- Squat: 3x2 at 85% 1RM
- Deadlift: 3x2 at 85% 1RM
- Bench: 3x3 at 78–80% 1RM
- Overhead press: 3x3 at 78–80% 1RM
- Accessory: 2–3 exercises, 2–3 sets
- Cooling: dedicated cooling protocol; ensure symptom monitoring

Week 12
- Deload/Consolidation
- Squat: 3x3 at 75–78% 1RM
- Deadlift: 3x3 at 75–78% 1RM
- Bench: 3x4 at 72–75% 1RM
- Overhead press: 3x4 at 72–75% 1RM
- Accessory: 2 exercises, 2x6
- Performance check: assess 1RM or estimated 1RM if safe, note gains
- Recovery: plan for ongoing maintenance after week 12

Exercise selections and progression notes
- Core bone-loading compound lifts: back squat, deadlift (conventional or sumo), bench press, overhead press
- Hip-dominant movements: Romanian deadlifts, hip thrusts, glute bridges (especially for posterior chain and hip stability)
- Upper back and lats: barbell rows, Pendlay rows, lat pulldown variations
- Accessory lower-body: Bulgarian split squats, step-ups, lunges (forward or reverse)
- Core and anti-rotation: Pallof press, side planks, suspended planks
- Mobility and warm-up: hip flexor mobility, ankle dorsiflexion, thoracic spine mobility; prehab protocols for shoulder health

Nutrition and supplement considerations
- Protein: aim 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, distributed across 3–5 meals; include 25–40 g protein per major meal
- Calcium and vitamin D: ensure 1000–1200 mg calcium daily (adjust for age/needs); vitamin D 800–2000 IU/day or as advised by clinician
- Peri-workout fueling: protein + carb 30–60 minutes pre-workout if energy is a concern; post-workout protein 20–40 g with some carbohydrates within 60 minutes
- Hydration: aim for baseline 2–3 L/day, increasing on training days; monitor urine color
- Bone-supportive foods: leafy greens, fortified dairy or alternatives, lean proteins, whole grains, healthy fats
- Supplements: discuss with GP; consider calcium/vitamin D as needed, omega-3s for anti-inflammatory benefits, magnesium for sleep and muscle function

Heat management and symptom monitoring
- Avoid any fasted, high-intensity sessions in heated environments
- Schedule hard sessions in cooler parts of the day or climate-controlled gym
- After hard sessions, implement cooling: 15–20 minutes of light activity (cycling/walking), cold towels, fan exposure, and air-conditioned recovery space
- Monitor symptoms: track hot flashes, night sweats, sleep quality, energy, and perceived exertion; if symptoms worsen, scale back intensity or volume for 1–2 weeks and re-test

Programming notes for the trainer
- Baseline testing: consider re-testing 1RM in week 1 and again in week 12 if the client is ready and symptoms permit
- Technique checks: ensure squat depth and bar path are safe; use tempo cues to maximize bone-loading stimulus
- Auto-regulation: if energy or temperature is high on a given day, reduce load by 5–10% or drop to 2x5 instead of 4x5, and avoid grinding reps
- Fatigue management: implement optional mobility/movement flow on rest days; include light conditioning if feasible to aid recovery
- Injury prevention: prioritize thoracic mobility, shoulder health, and hip mobility; address any niggles early

Progress tracking
- Track weekly loads, reps, and RPE for main lifts; aim for consistent progression in volume or intensity
- Log hot flash/night sweat occurrences and cooling efficacy to tailor session timing and intensity
- Review 4-week blocks for adjustments; if plateaus occur, consider microcycles with slightly higher volume and slightly lower intensity to stimulate adaptation

Safety and GP considerations
- If any significant health changes occur (cardiovascular symptoms, dizziness, chest pain), halt training and consult healthcare professionals
- Maintain communication with the client’s GP regarding perimenopausal symptoms and exercise plan

If you’d like, I can tailor the plan further to specific equipment available, preferred exercise substitutions (e.g., replacing barbell squats with goblet squats if needed), and a more precise weekly schedule with exact day assignments and warm-up routines.
